barrier_tree_analysis_for_main.question: Can barrier count inside one Add tree be reduced (e.g. 4-way unrolled with single barrier after a group) to beat H3?
barrier_tree_analysis_for_main.answer: H3 already achieves the theoretical minimum: 0 intermediate barriers for the Add chain (in-order V-pipe handles RAW — correctness confirmed), 1 barrier before ReduceSum. A 4-way unrolled tree (3 Adds per level vs 2-way's 1 Add per level) has fewer levels (log4 vs log2) but MORE total Adds (3*log4(N) = 1.5*log2(N)). With 0 intermediate barriers, level count is irrelevant to barrier cost — only total Add count matters, and 2-way pairwise is optimal (minimum Adds for a binary reduction). 4-way would only win if per-level barriers were required (reducing barrier count from log2(N/S) to log4(N/S)), but H3's barrier-free chain already removes that term. Conclusion: no clearly better single-variable form found; H3 is the right shape. If short-span still loses, the remaining lever is ReduceSum's internal cost on short spans (not barrier count).
